sections.h2: What the Webster County Clerk's office in Dixon handles
sections.html:
Everything on paper that touches land in the county passes through the Clerk's counter at the Webster County Courthouse, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Recordings, voter registration, marriage licenses, and title lien statements share the line 270-639-7006, vehicle registration answers at 270-639-7005, and the fax number is 270-639-7029.

The same office licenses vehicles, runs elections, issues notary bonds, and processes delinquent real estate taxes. For someone selling a house it matters three times: when the buyer's deed is recorded, when a paid-off mortgage needs its release put on the record, and when a bill misses the Sheriff's April 15 cutoff and lands at the Clerk with a lien attached.

Land records here reach back to 1786, though the county itself dates from 1860. Disputes about records or fines go to the courts, at 270-639-9160 or 270-639-9300.

All of them are free to view, a service that began August 1, 2010. Staff are still scanning and indexing older books, so coverage keeps growing. Here is what can be viewed:

  • Deeds: every book from 1860 (Book 1) forward, plus deeds of partition for 1893 through 2017.
  • Mortgages from 1972 and encumbrances from 1974.
  • Plats, all current ones, with the oldest in the two Processioner books covering 1861 to 1912.
  • Wills and marriage records from 1860, and every fixture filing.
  • Miscellaneous records starting with Book 20 in 1939.

A link beside the land records leads to a delinquent tax lookup. Before listing, search your name in the index and confirm each paid mortgage shows a release. Then check for liens, lis pendens notices, and judgments, because a title examiner who finds an unreleased one late in the process can push a closing back.

Since January 1, 2020, Webster County has followed the Property Records Industry Association layout rules, as every Kentucky county clerk does. A document that ignores them can be rejected at the window.

  • White 20 lb paper, 8 1/2 by 11 preferred and 8 1/2 by 14 accepted, with no watermarks.
  • One-sided printing, no staples or binding, no raised seals, no highlighter.
  • Leave 3 inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, with 1 inch margins everywhere else.
  • Black ink with dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or similar, at most 9 lines per inch.

A closing attorney usually deals with this, so most sellers never see the rules. Trouble comes mainly when a family transfer is typed up from a template.

These fees took effect January 1, 2020. Every document pays a flat charge, plus $3.00 for each page after the fifth.

A mortgage recorded together with an assignment costs $126.00 for up to 30 pages. Call for an exact total before mailing a packet.

What goes into a deed is set by two Kentucky statutes, KRS 382.135 and KRS 382.110. and both direct the clerk to turn away a deed that is incomplete. File in the county where the land sits, or where most of it sits.

  • Grantor and grantee names in full, each with a mailing address.
  • The whole price, certified under oath before a notary by both sides. For a gift, the certificate says so and gives an estimated fair cash value.
  • The address where the bill for the transfer year should go.
  • How the seller took title: the earlier deed's book, page and recording date, or a note explaining an inheritance.

Inherited land, whether through a will or intestacy, needs one more paper. The personal representative must give each county clerk where land is held an affidavit naming the heirs and valuing each parcel before the estate closes. If a defective deed is recorded anyway, the filing still gives notice to others, though a title insurer may raise the flaw.

sections.h2: Kentucky transfer tax on a sale
sections.html:
The seller pays Kentucky 50 cents per $500 of value, and any leftover partial block is rounded up. The rule sits in KRS 142.050. The Clerk figures it from the deed, takes payment up front, and stamps the date and amount onto the deed.

Collection happens once per transaction. Five percent stays with the Clerk, and the remainder goes quarterly to the county treasurer's general fund.

Among the exempt transfers are foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, divorce transfers, partitions, corrective deeds, deeds that only secure a debt, and parent to child gifts with nominal payment. With no stated price the tax follows the open-market estimate.

sections.h2: Who else in Dixon should a seller call?
sections.html:
A sale touches several desks in the same courthouse. The PVA, at 270-639-7016, holds the assessment and parcel data and processes ownership changes for tax purposes. The Sheriff, at 270-639-5067, collects the current year's property tax. The Clerk, at 270-639-7006, records the deed and takes any older delinquent bills. Three short calls before you list will get you every payoff and status answer you need.

The county was created in 1860 out of Henderson, Hopkins, and Union counties, which is why the deed index starts with Book 1 that year. For a very old chain of title, ask the Clerk where an earlier link should be searched. Every city in the county records deeds at this one office.

sections.h2: Recording deadlines that can affect a sale
sections.html:
KRS 382.110 sets two clocks. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must record it within 45 days of signing. A person receiving a deed from a court-appointed commissioner gets five business days. When you are the seller in one of these transactions, ask the other party for proof of filing before you consider the matter finished.

Other filings arrive too: a mortgage release to clear the old loan, an affidavit of descent that records who inherited, and releases of mechanic liens or lis pendens notices that otherwise cloud the title. After April 15 the Clerk also receives certificates of delinquency from the Sheriff, so request a payoff on any earlier year before you list.

Webster County has 4,923 households, 73.8 percent of them owner-occupied, and a median home value of $112,900. Homes that are inherited, need work, or carry liens often go to cash buyers as-is, and recording works the same way for those sales.

faqs.q: What is the best way to file a deed with the Webster County Clerk?
faqs.a: Bring or send it to 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., after confirming the total at 270-639-7006.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Webster County deed?
faqs.a: $50.00 for the deed, and $3.00 more for every page over five. A mortgage release is $46.00; a certified copy is $5.00.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax calculated for a Webster County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes 50 cents per $500 of value, rounded up. The Clerk collects it before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is there free online access to Webster County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Clerk's website offers free searches of deeds from 1860, mortgages from 1972, plats, wills, and a delinquent tax lookup.

faqs.q: How soon must a deed in lieu of foreclosure be recorded in Webster County?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of signing, under KRS 382.110. A commissioner's deed must be filed within five business days after the grantee receives it.
